tex_content.html:
There is a universal $\varepsilon _0>0$ such that $\varepsilon \leq \varepsilon _0$ implies \[ \begin{split} \widetilde V_x(W_{\mathrm{lg}}(\tau _1)) & \leq \int _{\widetilde U(\tau _1)\cap \{ |Z|\geq (8\sqrt\varepsilon )^{-1}\} } \tau _1^{-n/2}e^{-\widetilde l(Z,\tau _1)} {\mathcal J}(Z,\tau _1)\, dZ\\ & \leq \varepsilon ^{n/2}. \end{split} \]

Proof

\sketch ↗ prop:reduced-volume-integrand-monotone Monotonicity of the reduced-volume density bounds its pullback by $2^ne^{-|Z|^2}$. Hence the integral is at most the Gaussian tail outside the ball of radius $(8\sqrt\varepsilon )^{-1}$. Comparing that ball with the centered cube of half-side $(8\sqrt{n\varepsilon })^{-1}$ gives

\[ \widetilde V_x(W_{\mathrm{lg}}(\tau _1)) \leq (4\pi )^{n/2}\frac n2 e^{-1/(64n\varepsilon )}. \]

For sufficiently small universal $\varepsilon _0$, this is at most $\varepsilon ^{n/2}$.

□
